summary: Versions 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 went live, and 0.4.2 follows this report, at https://agmgd-on-ipo-monitor-ba4eccd0.fly.dev on 2026-11-16. The service can now watch the SEC's list of the company's filings and read the final IPO price from the cover of a final prospectus, only if every check passes; the public repository explains how the whole system works, including where AI is involved. The filings watch is live and switched off: it needs a contact address for sec.gov that only the owner can put on the machine, so the service's own client has not talked to EDGAR yet. Not run for that reason: the watch on the live site, and the price read from a real final prospectus of another company. Failed: setting the About box of the repository (the agent's GitHub access cannot change repository settings; nothing was changed). The owner's look at the page on a phone is still not run.
delivered: A filings watch (edgar.py): every ten minutes the service asks EDGAR for the registrant's filing list; strict reading of the answer; a failure becomes the 'unavailable' state and keeps what was known.

On the page: a 'filings' line in the status block (latest filing, or a notice when a prospectus newer than the one the page reads exists) and a FILINGS panel with the latest filings in plain words, linked to sec.gov, same-day filings of one form on one line (key f).

The final price read by the service from the cover of a final prospectus (Form 424B4 or 424B1) as the fact pricing.ipo_price labeled FILED, with the cover quoted. Refused unless the cover names the company, is not preliminary, gives dollars and cents, states a total equal to price times the shares on the same cover, and the price is within half the low and twice the high of the filed range.
A filed price replaces a price recorded from the press (Facts.plus with a document and replacing).
The watch cannot break the page: if rendering fails with the filing list, the page is rendered without it; the market panel is untouched.

SEC_CONTACT and IPO_FILINGS settings. The address is sent to data.sec.gov and www.sec.gov only, never logged, never shown, kept out of repr. An unusable address switches the watch off and logs why without the value.
deploy/start.sh reads known secret names from /data/secrets.env (root-only), never printing a value. The boot loop on the machine was restarted once to pick it up.
/health reports the filings watch: state, source, time of the last check, latest filing, final prospectus, whether its price was read.

HOW-IT-WORKS.md: the path of a figure, who does what, where AI is involved (build time, the coding agent) and where it is not (the live service runs no model), what runs by itself, the path of a change, the GitHub workflows one by one, the loop method. Two diagrams.
README rewritten as a front page: live link, CI and CodeQL badges, current screenshots, panels, labels, workflows, release path, loop method. CONTRIBUTING updated.
Version 0.3.2, the fix found at the market open, deployed at the start of the loop once the owner confirmed D-016.
Three deployments on the existing machine before this report (0.3.2, 0.4.0, 0.4.1), each healthy within seconds; 0.4.2 is deployed right after it.
decisions: Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-16: D-016, a release whose checks all pass is deployed without asking ('Oui, déploie seul'). Access, exposure and infrastructure changes still need approval.
Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-16: before the first trade, only the filings watch and the final prospectus; deployment by GitHub, alerts and history after it ('ok go').
Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-16: document the public repository well, the link, the workflows, and how the system works including the part of AI (D-026).
Proposed, D-023: the service publishes by itself only what passes every check; from a final prospectus, only the price on the cover.
Proposed, D-024: a price read from the final prospectus replaces a price recorded from the press.
Proposed, D-025: the contact address lives in a root-only file on the machine; an unusable address switches the watch off instead of stopping the service.
Assumed and not carried out: the agent would set the About box of the repository. Its GitHub access cannot change repository settings, so nothing was changed.
Assumed: filings of one form made on one day share one line in the panel; eight lines are shown.
Still proposed from Loop 002: D-017 to D-022.

The agent's GitHub access cannot change repository settings: the About box stays empty until the owner fills it.
CI cannot reach the machine: deployment stays manual, from the coding agent's session (planned for the next loop, with the owner's approval of that access).
